newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut unemployment rate at 5.2 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut unemployment rate at 5.2 pct in April.

text.p: Connecticut's unemployment rate increased by three-tenths of a percentage point to 5.2 percent in April, the state Department of Labor reported on Wednesday.
An increase in Connecticut's nonfarm employment in April was countered by an increase in the unemployment rate. There was a gain of 1,300 jobs over the month to 1,599,900.
In April, an estimated 89,800 Connecticut residents were unemployed. The number is up 4,100 from March's figure and down 8,700 from April 1996.

Nonfarm jobs have increased by 23,000 since April 1996, when they numbered 1,576,900. The unemployment rate was down five-tenths of a percentage point from April 1996 and was three-tenths of a percentage above the national rate of 4.9 percent.
Average weekly initial unemployment claims for first-time filers increased by 455, to 4,335 during the month. April's figure was up 61 from the year before.
Job gains were reported in government, including Indian tribal government, up 3,200; transportation, communication and utilties, up 500; manufacturing, up 400; and construction and mining, up 300.
Decreases were reported in wholesale and retail trade, down 2,600; services, down 400; and finance, insurance and real estate, down 100. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
